cards.html: This skill links fractions, decimals and percentages, and covers percentage change, the single most used calculation in economics.

Digits after the point are tenths, hundredths, thousandths: 0.375 = 3/10 + 7/100 + 5/1000 = 375/1000 = 3/8.

  • × 10 moves the point one place right: 0.375 × 10 = 3.75. ÷ 10 moves it left: 3.75 ÷ 10 = 0.375.
  • To multiply decimals, ignore the points, multiply, then put back as many decimal places as the two numbers had together: 0.3 × 0.04: 3 × 4 = 12, three places → 0.012.
  • To divide by a decimal, shift both numbers until the divisor is whole: 4.5 ÷ 0.15 = 450 ÷ 15 = 30.

Per cent means "out of 100". So 35% = 35/100 = 0.35.

FromToHowExample
PercentageDecimal÷ 1007.5% = 0.075
DecimalPercentage× 1000.4 = 40%
FractionDecimalDivide top by bottom3/8 = 0.375
DecimalFractionOver 10, 100 or 1000, then simplify0.45 = 45/100 = 9/20

Worth knowing by heart: 1/2 = 0.5 = 50%, 1/4 = 25%, 3/4 = 75%, 1/5 = 20%, 1/10 = 10%, 1/3 ≈ 33.3%, 1/8 = 12.5%.

cards.s: Percentages of an amount and the multiplier
cards.html:
To find a percentage of an amount, multiply by the decimal: 15% of 240 = 0.15 × 240 = 36.

To increase or decrease by a percentage, use one multiplier:

ChangeMultiplierExample
Increase by 20%1.2050 × 1.2 = 60
Decrease by 20%0.8050 × 0.8 = 40
Increase by 3.5%1.035200 × 1.035 = 207
Add 19% VAT1.19100 × 1.19 = 119

Repeated changes multiply: 5% growth two years running is 1.05 × 1.05 = 1.1025, a 10.25% rise, not 10%. This is compounding.

Percentage change = (new − old) / old × 100.

price 80 -> 92:
  (92 - 80)/80 × 100
  = 12/80 × 100 = 15% rise
GDP 500 -> 485:
  (485 - 500)/500 × 100
  = -3%  (a 3% fall)

Always divide by the old value.

Reverse percentage: a price after 25% off is 60. What was it before? The multiplier was 0.75, so the original = 60 ÷ 0.75 = 80. (Not 60 + 25% of 60 = 75.)

Percent vs percentage points: interest rates going from 2% to 3% rose by 1 percentage point, but by 50 per cent (1/2 × 100).

1. Write 0.06 as a percentage and as a fraction.
  2. Write 5/8 as a decimal.
  3. 0.7 × 0.03
  4. 6 ÷ 0.2
  5. 12% of 350
  6. Increase 640 by 15%.
  7. A price goes from 25 to 20. What is the percentage change?
  8. After a 20% pay rise, a salary is 42,000. What was it before?
  9. Prices rise 10% one year and fall 10% the next. Are they back where they started?
  10. Unemployment goes from 4% to 5%. Give the change in percentage points and in per cent.

🔒 Answers: try the questions first, then tap to show

1: 6%, 6/100 = 3/50. 2: 0.625. 3: 0.021. 4: 30. 5: 42. 6: 640 × 1.15 = 736. 7: −5/25 = −20%. 8: 42,000 ÷ 1.2 = 35,000. 9: No: 1.1 × 0.9 = 0.99, so 1% lower. 10: 1 percentage point; 25 per cent.

t: Percentages of an amount and the multiplier

quiz.q: A price falls from 50 to 42. What is the percentage change? (Negative for a fall.)
After a 25% discount a jacket costs 90. What was the original price?
A 10% rise followed by a 10% fall brings a price back to where it started.
The interest rate rises from 2% to 3%. Which statement is right?
o: It rose by 1 percentage point, which is a 50% rise
quiz.why: 3 − 2 = 1 percentage point; relative to 2, that is a 50% rise.

concept.q: Sales fell 50% last year and rose 50% this year. Compared with two years ago, they are…
concept.why: 0.5 × 1.5 = 0.75. The 50% rise works on a smaller base than the 50% fall did.

concept.q: A price including 20% VAT is 96. Find the price before VAT.
concept.why: The 20% is of the price BEFORE VAT, not of 96. 96 = 1.2 × P, so P = 80.

concept.q: x% of y is equal to y% of x.
concept.why: x/100 × y = y/100 × x. So 8% of 50 is the same as 50% of 8, which is 4.

concept.q: 0.5% is the same as one half.
concept.why: Myth. 0.5% = 0.005, which is one two-hundredth. One half is 50%.

concept.q: Three 10% rises in a row add up to a 30% rise.
concept.why: 1.1³ = 1.331, so it's a 33.1% rise. It is always more than 30%, because each rise works on a bigger base.
